claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

Let's start with the basics:

**How many children would you like to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I have one child - Alex, who's 17 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! Since Alex is 17 years old, I need to ask a few more questions to determine your eligibility.

**Is Alex currently in approved education (such as A-levels, Scottish Highers, or an equivalent full-time course) or approved training (such as an unpaid, employer-provided training course)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in any education or training at the moment. They finished school but aren't doing A-levels or anything like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. Since Alex is 17 and not currently in approved education or training, there are still a couple of ways you might remain eligible for Child Benefit.

**Has Alex registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services since leaving education?**

(If they have, you may be able to claim Child Benefit for up to 20 weeks.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex hasn't registered with any careers service or the armed forces. They just finished school and haven't signed up for anything like that yet.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. I have a couple more questions to check all the possibilities:

**Does Alex currently do any of the following?**

1. Work for 24 hours or more per week
2. Have an apprenticeship in England
3. Receive any benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, none of those apply. Alex doesn't work that much - they're not doing 24 hours a week or anything. They don't have an apprenticeship, and they're not getting any benefits in their own name either.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

**Do you live in the UK, and does Alex live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK and Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. One final question:

**Is anyone else currently receiving Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on what you've told me:

- Alex is 17 years old
- Alex is not in approved education or training
- Alex has not registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services
- Alex does not work 24+ hours per week, have an apprenticeship, or receive benefits in their own right
- You live in the UK and Alex lives with you
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex

Unfortunately, I have to inform you of the following:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on my assessment, **you are not currently eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

**For Alex (age 17):** Child Benefit normally continues for children aged 16-19 only if they remain in approved education or training. Alternatively, you can claim for up to 20 weeks if a 16 or 17 year old leaves education and registers with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services. Since Alex is not in approved education or training and hasn't registered with either of these services, the eligibility criteria for children aged 16 or over are not met.

**What you could do:**
If Alex were to:
- Enrol in approved education or training (such as A-levels, a BTEC, or another qualifying course), or
- Register with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services

...you may then become eligible to claim Child Benefit. If Alex does take either of these steps, you could make a new claim at that point.

I hope this helps clarify your situation. Is there anything else you'd like to know?
